A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GDR-learners work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix E report original comparisons on synthetic data, ACIC 2016, HC-MNIST, and IHDP100, including Wasserstein distances and log-probabilities.

after.justification: The original empirical comparisons remain, with additional colored-MNIST results, EMA sensitivity experiments, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The two-stage GDR objective remains unchanged. Appendix D adds image-specific architectural adaptations: FiLM conditioning, masked autoregressive flows, convolutional GAN/VAE networks, and U-Net diffusion denoisers. These extend the existing instantiations without replacing the framework.

E1.justification: v2 adds colored MNIST with five digit interventions and 10×10 RGB image outcomes, while retaining the earlier benchmarks. This substantially expands task coverage: unlike HC-MNIST’s image confounders and scalar outcomes, the new experiment generates image-valued potential outcomes.

E2.justification: The retained experiments compare the same plug-in, IPTW, RA, and GDR learners within the same generative-model families. The GANITE, NOFLITE, and DiffPO correspondences remain unchanged. Colored MNIST extends this comparator set to another task; revised training configurations are protocol changes.

E3.justification: v1 Table 5 becomes v2 Table 6 with substantive reported setting revisions: CGAN tuning changes from negative log-likelihood to generated-sample MSE, width searches expand, and optimizers, target widths, and learning rates change. CVAE and diffusion settings also change. New protocols include colored-MNIST preprocessing and 30,000/5,000 training/test samples, plus an EMA sweep. These disclosures do not establish that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds an EMA sensitivity study across three smoothing strengths, training sizes, and four generative families; an examination of HC-MNIST run dispersion and outliers; and a comparison of computational overhead. These substantially broaden the analyses beyond the retained ACIC full-versus-linear comparison and IHDP overlap discussion.

E5.justification: v2 supplements aggregate summaries with individual-run plots for HC-MNIST and colored MNIST, exposing dispersion and outliers directly. Existing experiments retain their stated replication counts, including 20 HC-MNIST runs and 100 IHDP splits. The new colored-MNIST experiment reports 10 runs; this is not an increase in replication of an earlier experiment.

E6.justification: CGAN results change in Figure 4, HC-MNIST Table 4, and IHDP100’s v1 Table 6/v2 Table 8. For example, HC-MNIST treatment 1 reports GDR-CGAN at 2.038±0.300, best among CGAN learners, in v1 versus 1.715±0.259, worst, in v2. These are revised results alongside changed settings, not a controlled performance gain. Colored-MNIST, EMA, and runtime results add substantial new evidence.

T1.justification: Appendix C removes Theorem 2’s separate weak-overlap assumption and changes the proof’s references to the overlap margin from weak to strong overlap, consistent with Section 3. The principal bounds and derivations remain intact. The new theoretical outlook largely restates existing definitions rather than introducing another theorem.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same principal claims: general Neyman-orthogonal learning of potential-outcome distributions, quasi-oracle efficiency, rate double robustness, four generative-model instantiations, and empirical effectiveness. The additional experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 adds discussion of whether the required nuisance convergence rates are achievable, including conditional-density dimensionality and possible manifold structure. Appendix E newly links HC-MNIST outliers to inverse-propensity weighting and the absence of finite-sample guarantees, contrasts colored MNIST’s overlap, and explains the two-stage runtime overhead.

D1.justification: Appendix D substantially expands architecture and hyperparameter documentation, including a separate colored-MNIST tuning table. Table 10 adds training times and GPU/CPU specifications. The advertised code location changes from an anonymous repository to an identified GitHub repository, with a README described in the reproducibility statement. Conversely, the explicit hypernetwork layer counts in v1 Table 5 disappear from v2 Table 6.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds a focused discussion connecting the method to augmented inverse-propensity weighting, semiparametric efficiency, and double machine learning. Additional references support convergence-rate discussion and image architectures. The central research gap and comparison with existing CDPO methods remain unchanged; several other reference changes are publication updates to the same works.

P1.justification: v2 adds a theoretical outlook, explanatory passages, and ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-usage statements. It revises Appendix D and converts the experiment subsections and conclusion into compact paragraph headings. Most existing prose and the overall argument remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the displays with an image-sample table, EMA curves, individual-run plots, and additional tuning, performance, and runtime tables. Figure 4’s CGAN axes change, and retained displays are relocated or renumbered, including ACIC Figure 5 becoming Figure 6. A layout regression makes Figure 6’s caption overlap the Section E.4 heading.

improvement.justification: The image-outcome evaluation and EMA, run-level stability, and runtime analyses provide useful evidence about applicability, sensitivity, and computational cost that v1 lacked. Expanded implementation information and clearer discussion of convergence requirements improve transparency. These gains outweigh limited regressions: v2 omits previously stated hypernetwork layer counts and introduces a caption-heading overlap. The improvement strengthens validation and documentation of the retained framework.
